A1-A2.headline: The Roots and Rules of Italian Fascism

pages.text: Italian fascism is the original fascist ideology. It was developed in Italy by Giovanni Gentile and Benito Mussolini. The National Fascist Party led the Kingdom of Italy from 1922 until 1943. This political movement changed Italy's history.
pages.caption: Benito Mussolini and fascist Blackshirt youth in 1935

evidence.articleCaption: Benito Mussolini and fascist Blackshirt youth in 1935

pages.text: The word fascismo comes from fascio, which means a bundle of sticks. This is related to the ancient Roman symbol of a bundle of rods tied around an axe. The symbol showed strength through unity.
pages.caption: Front page of the Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera on 11 November 1938: "Le leggi per la difesa della razza approvate dal Consiglio dei ministri" (English: "The laws for the defence of race approved by the Council of Ministers"). On the same day, the Racial Laws entered into force under the Italian Fascist regime, enacting the racial discrimination and persecution of Italian Jews.

On the same day, the Racial Laws entered into force under the Italian Fascist regime, enacting the racial discrimination and persecution of Italian Jews.

pages.text: The movement was based on strong Italian nationalism. It wanted to complete the incomplete Risorgimento to bring together Italian territories. Fascists also looked back to the imperial legacy of Ancient Rome.

pages.text: Italian fascism used a corporatist economic system. Employer and employee syndicates worked together with the state to set economic policy. Leaders called this economic system a third way.

pages.text: In 1925, the party declared that Italy would be a totalitarian state. Mussolini wanted to forge an authoritarian national state and create a new kind of citizen. The official formulation of the ideology was published in 1932.

B1-B2.headline: Origins and Structure of Italian Fascism

pages.text: Italian fascism is the original fascist ideology developed in Italy by Giovanni Gentile and Benito Mussolini. It was associated with political parties led by Mussolini, including the National Fascist Party that governed the Kingdom of Italy from 1922 until 1943.
pages.caption: Benito Mussolini and fascist Blackshirt youth in 1935

pages.text: The term fascismo derives from fascio, meaning bundle of sticks, from the Latin word fasces. The fascists associated the term with the ancient Roman fasces, a bundle of rods tied around an axe as a symbol of authority and strength through unity.
pages.caption: Front page of the Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera on 11 November 1938: "Le leggi per la difesa della razza approvate dal Consiglio dei ministri" (English: "The laws for the defence of race approved by the Council of Ministers"). On the same day, the Racial Laws entered into force under the Italian Fascist regime, enacting the racial discrimination and persecution of Italian Jews.

evidence.articleCaption: Front page of the Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera on 11 November 1938: "Le leggi per la difesa della razza approvate dal Consiglio dei ministri" (English: "The laws for the defence of race approved by the Council of Ministers"). On the same day, the Racial Laws entered into force under the Italian Fascist regime, enacting the racial discrimination and persecution of Italian Jews.

pages.text: Rooted in intense Italian nationalism and militarism, the movement sought to complete the nationalist Risorgimento project by incorporating unredeemed territories. Fascists claimed modern Italy was an heiress to the imperial legacy of Ancient Rome to create vital space.
pages.caption: Roman she-wolf, symbol of the founding legend of Rome

evidence.articleCaption: Roman she-wolf, symbol of the founding legend of Rome

pages.text: Italian fascism promoted a corporatist economic system where employer and employee syndicates were linked together to work alongside the state. This system aimed to resolve class conflict through collaboration while opposing both classical liberalism and socialism.
pages.caption: Map indicating Italian-inhabited territories (bright green) within the Austro-Hungarian Empire in 1911

pages.text: In 1925, the party declared the fascist state would be totalitarian, aiming to forge an authoritarian national state and create politically active citizens. The official formulation was published in 1932 as The Doctrine of Fascism.

Although Mussolini initially denied antisemitism within the party, Italian laws eventually became explicitly antisemitic due to pressure from Nazi Germany during the latter half of the 1930s, leading to the promulgation of the Italian racial laws.

Italian fascism represents the foundational fascist ideology formulated by Giovanni Gentile and Benito Mussolini. It found institutional expression through the National Fascist Party and the Republican Fascist Party during their respective periods of governance in the Kingdom of Italy and the Italian Social Republic.

pages.text: Etymologically derived from fascio, the terminology recalls the ancient Roman fasces, symbolizing civic magistrate authority and strength through unity. The organizational lineage traces from the Fasces of Revolutionary Action through the Italian Fasces of Combat to the National Fascist Party.
pages.caption: Front page of the Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera on 11 November 1938: "Le leggi per la difesa della razza approvate dal Consiglio dei ministri" (English: "The laws for the defence of race approved by the Council of Ministers"). On the same day, the Racial Laws entered into force under the Italian Fascist regime, enacting the racial discrimination and persecution of Italian Jews.

evidence.articleCaption: Front page of the Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera on 11 November 1938: "Le leggi per la difesa della razza approvate dal Consiglio dei ministri" (English: "The laws for the defence of race approved by the Council of Ministers"). On the same day, the Racial Laws entered into force under the Italian Fascist regime, enacting the racial discrimination and persecution of Italian Jews.

pages.text: Ideologically rooted in ultra-nationalism, national syndicalism, and irredentism, the movement sought to finalize the incomplete Risorgimento project by incorporating unredeemed territories. Proponents asserted an imperial continuity with Ancient Rome to justify territorial expansion and secure vital space within the Mediterranean basin.
pages.caption: Roman she-wolf, symbol of the founding legend of Rome

evidence.articleCaption: Roman she-wolf, symbol of the founding legend of Rome

pages.text: The regime established a corporatist economic framework that linked employer and employee syndicates to coordinate national economic policy alongside the state. Positioned as a third alternative to capitalism and Marxism, this structure endeavored to neutralize class conflict.
pages.caption: Map indicating Italian-inhabited territories (bright green) within the Austro-Hungarian Empire in 1911

evidence.articleCaption: Map indicating Italian-inhabited territories (bright green) within the Austro-Hungarian Empire in 1911

pages.text: By 1925, the party embraced totalitarianism, utilizing it to construct an authoritarian national state designed to cultivate politically active fascist citizens. This totalitarian framework received its definitive philosophical formulation in The Doctrine of Fascism, ghostwritten by Giovanni Gentile.

While early fascist rhetoric rejected certain racial doctrines and antisemitism, alignment with Nazi Germany in the late 1930s precipitated the institutionalization of explicit racial laws and discriminatory state policies directed against Jews, minority linguistic groups, and populations in occupied territories.
